title: Senior AI Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As an Senior AI Engineer at GitLab, you'll help build the foundation for GitLab's transformation into an AI-first company. Reporting to the Director, Enterprise AI, you'll be a hands-on technical leader responsible for delivering internal AI-powered solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>Building fast matters, but it's not enough on its own. This role starts with understanding the real problem: mapping how work moves across teams, tools, and handoffs, identifying the true constraint, and validating whether AI is the right solution before you begin development. From there, you'll take ownership from discovery through deployment, combining strong engineering skills with systems thinking and business understanding.</p> <p>Your initial focus will span Sales, Marketing, and Customer Support, where you will embed AI solutions into key systems and workflows. This role offers the opportunity to shape how GitLab team members work, improve flow across the organization, and help advance our mission in a remote, asynchronous, and values-driven environment.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Diagnose business problems before building solutions. Map workflows, identify constraints, and confirm whether AI is the right intervention. Be prepared to say "this doesn't need AI" when that's the honest answer.</li> <li>Own AI initiatives end-to-end, from stakeholder discovery and technical design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.</li> <li>Design, develop, and ship AI-powered solutions quickly, delivering working prototypes in days, not months, with a focus on practical outcomes and measurable business value.</li> <li>Improve organizational flow by building solutions that reduce bottlenecks, shorten lead times, and increase throughput. Measure success using flow metrics alongside adoption and ROI.</li> <li>Integrate AI capabilities into existing systems and workflows using APIs, orchestration tools, and modern AI platforms, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, where appropriate. The right tool wins, whether that's custom code, a platform, or a well-crafted prompt.</li> <li>Be Customer Zero: leverage and showcase GitLab's AI offerings wherever possible, feeding real-world usage insights back to R&D.</li> <li>Partner closely with stakeholders across functions to understand the real constraints. Ask the right questions, bridge technical and non-technical perspectives, and align on outcomes before jumping to solutions.</li> <li>Define and track success through business metrics, flow metrics, and feedback loops that make performance visible and actionable.</li> <li>Contribute to technical direction by evaluating tools, documenting patterns, and creating reusable foundations that help the team scale its impact.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A Technologist at Heart - </strong>Genuinely invested in technology, the foundational and the cutting-edge in equal measure. You're as energised by a well-designed API integration as you are by the latest foundation model release. You reach for the simplest solution that solves the problem well, rather than forcing new technology when proven approaches would do. AI is a powerful part of your toolkit, but it sits on top of solid engineering fundamentals, not in place of them.</li> <li><strong>Competent, Confident Coding Skills - </strong>You can build working solutions end-to-end, write clean and maintainable code, and debug effectively. Whether your skills were honed in a traditional engineering role, through building automations, or shipping side projects, what matters is that you can deliver production-quality work independently.</li> <li><strong>AI</strong><strong> & LLM </strong><strong>Technical Depth - </strong>Strong proficiency in at least one modern scripting language (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar) and a solid understanding of REST APIs, GraphQL, and integration patterns. Deep, practical experience with modern AI technologies, specifically: Prompt engineering as a core discipline: designing effective system prompts, managing context windows, structuring multi-turn interactions, evaluating output quality, and iterating systematically on prompt design.</li> <li><strong>Model selection and cost-performance trade-offs: </strong>understanding when a smaller fine-tuned model outperforms a general-purpose large one, when RAG is the right architecture versus expanding the context window, and how to make principled decisions about capability versus cost.</li> <li><strong>Agentic architecture patterns: </strong>tool use, multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop designs, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and production-grade reliability patterns.Practical fluency across the LLM ecosystem: hands-on experience with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, open-source alternatives, and the judgment to know which to reach for and when.</li> <li><strong>AI Safety & Risk Awareness - </strong>You think critically about how the solutions you build could be exploited, misused, or produce unintended consequences. You know how to design appropriate guardrails (input validation, output filtering, access controls, prompt injection defences, and data leakage prevention) and you treat these as first-class engineering concerns.</li> <li><strong>Systems Thinking & Diagnostic Rigour - </strong>The ability to look at a complex process and see the constraint. Comfortable mapping how work flows end-to-end, identifying bottlenecks, and tracing problems to root causes before proposing solutions. You instinctively ask "what's actually blocking flow here?" before asking "what model should I use?"</li> <li><strong>Business System Expertise - </strong>Familiarity with the landscape of enterprise business systems, CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (Marketo), support platforms (Zendesk), integration and orchestration tools (Workato), AI platforms (Relevance AI), and enterprise search and knowledge tools (Glean). You don't need deep experience with all of these, but to understand what they do, how they fit together, and be willing to build with and across them. A strong understanding of enterprise data models and workflows is essential.</li> <li><strong>Broad Functional Understanding - </strong>Ability to have meaningful conversations with stakeholders across diverse domains and quickly understand their unique needs.</li> <li><strong>End-to-End Ownership - </strong>Track record of owning complex initiatives from discovery through delivery. Comfortable operating with ambiguity and driving to measurable outcomes independently.</li> <li><strong>Product Mindset - </strong>Ability to scope MVPs, prioritise ruthlessly, and deliver iteratively. In addition, consider adoption, user experience, and business outcomes.</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Preferred requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with GitLab platform and CI/CD workflows</li> <li>Background in consulting, solutions engineering, or customer-facing technical roles</li> <li>Familiarity with value stream mapping, flow metrics, or Theory of Constraints thinking</li> <li>Experience with low-code/no-code orchestration tools (n8n, Make, Workato) alongside custom development</li> <li>Previous startup or high-growth company experience</li> <li>Experience mentoring or leading technical projects with junior engineers</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>You will join the Enterprise Technology & AI team. We're the backbone of the organisation, driving transformation in how GitLab team members make decisions, operate at scale, and deliver results for our customers.</p> <p>We believe the best AI solutions start with understanding the system, not the technology. We value people who think in constraints and flow, who build with conviction, and who never stop learning. We work in an all-remote, asynchronous setting, guided by GitLab's values of collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.</li> <li value="2">Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.</li> <li value="3">Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate with <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/">Product</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/">Development</a>, <a Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> value="8">Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.</li> <li value="2">Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.</li> <li value="4">Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.</li> <li value="5">Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.</li> <li value="7">Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.</li> <li value="8">Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most title: Senior Assigned Support Engineer (EMEA)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be a trusted technical advisor to GitLab’s largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, helping them avoid operational disruption and get the most from GitLab. You’ll combine deep Linux systems expertise, GitLab and CI/CD knowledge, and a proactive support mindset to understand each customer’s environment, anticipate and prevent issues, and solve complex technical and business challenges. In a typical week, you might be prioritizing strategic blockers with customer stakeholders, partnering with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to drive defect resolution and influence the roadmap, or diving into code, logs, and tools like strace to troubleshoot performance issues. Your impact in the first year will be measured by customer trust, reduced critical incidents, and clear, reusable support content that empowers customers and GitLab teams alike.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Provide technical support to our largest Self-managed, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab.com customers, ensuring their GitLab environments remain stable and performant.</li> <li value="2">Troubleshoot and resolve complex, critical, and sensitive support issues using tools like Zendesk, logs, and Linux utilities such as strace, through email and video conferencing.</li> <li value="3">Build strong, proactive relationships with key customer stakeholders, helping them prioritize and address their most important technical blockers.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate with <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/product/">Product</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/development/">Development</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure/">Infrastructure</a>, <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-success/">Customer Success</a>, and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/sales/">Sales</a> teams to drive bug fixes, influence feature development, and help shape product goals and roadmap.</li> <li value="5">Act as a technical expert on GitLab and CI/CD implementations, advising customers on how incidents and service interruptions impact their workflows and how to mitigate them.</li> <li value="6">Create and improve support content, including documentation and knowledge articles, to help customers and GitLab team members resolve issues more efficiently.</li> <li value="7">Partner closely with Support Engineering team members through <a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w">pairing sessions</a> and <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart">stable counterpart</a> relationships to share knowledge and solve problems together.</li> <li value="8">Contribute to team growth by participating in hiring processes, including reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Background managing complex, customer facing support cases end to end, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution.</li> <li value="2">Advanced troubleshooting skills with the ability to investigate ambiguous, multi-layered technical issues and identify root causes across applications, infrastructure, and integrations.</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge (LFCE or RHCE equivalent), including performance analysis and low-level debugging tools.</li> <li value="4">Practical experience with GitLab and continuous integration / continuous delivery (CI/CD), including how different deployment models and outages affect customers.</li> <li value="5">Ability to write and maintain clear, reusable support content such as knowledge articles, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides.</li> <li value="6">Proficiency with scripting languages (such as Ruby or Bash) and familiarity with model-view-controller (MVC) frameworks, preferably Ruby on Rails.</li> <li value="7">Effective communication skills for explaining complex technical topics to audiences with varying technical backgrounds and for building rapport with customer stakeholders.</li> <li value="8">Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless platforms, with openness to applying transferable skills from related domains.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Support team is a fully distributed, global group across the AMER, EMEA, and APAC regions, focused on helping customers get the most from GitLab by troubleshooting complex issues and digging into code and logs to understand why something is not working as expected. As an Assigned Support Engineer, you’ll be part of our broader Support Engineering organization, working closely with other Support Engineers through regular pairing sessions, 1:1s, coffee chats, and Slack conversations to stay connected while collaborating asynchronously across time zones. We balance autonomy with accountability, giving you flexibility to structure your shift in a way that fits your life while ensuring we can reliably address customer issues. Thanks to GitLab’s <a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/all-remote/values/#transparency">Transparency</a> value, you can see what we are working on in our<a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/"> Support Team</a> page. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Identify sources of friction across GitLab's software development lifecycle and scope agentic solutions to address them, turning vague pain points into concrete, buildable proposals.</li> <li>Design and build reliable AI-powered systems that follow step-by-step workflows, use tools and safety checks, and correct errors before taking engineering action — the kind of output you can actually trust with real engineering decisions.</li> <li>Build and maintain evaluation tools that judge agent output on correctness, constraint compliance, and cost, not on whether it merely "seems to work."</li> <li>Work across GitLab's codebase as each problem requires, going wherever the friction actually is rather than staying inside one service or product area.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to identify generated code that may fail under concurrency, at scale, or across self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant deployments, catching failures before they reach customers.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group, sharing roadmaps, findings, and reusable agent tooling</li> <li>Take ownership of a greenfield problem space from day one, helping shape a proven internal fix into a capability GitLab could offer customers externally, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience building agentic or large language model-based systems — multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery patterns — and making them reliable in production, not treated as one-off prompts or demonstrations.</li> <li>A track record of working autonomously in unfamiliar codebases, getting oriented quickly, and driving solutions through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems knowledge, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, in that order of team priority, and the ability to read and modify code in the other languages.</li> <li>Helpful experience includes shipping autonomous agents that complete real tasks from start to finish; improving build systems, release processes, review workflows, or other parts of the software development lifecycle; and working with globally distributed teams, large language model workload costs, or production constraints across on-premises, air-gapped, single-tenant, and software-as-a-service deployments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. It operates like a startup — no dedicated product manager, no pre-set backlog — and solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who'd rather go find the next problem than be handed one, and who want a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <p> </p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You will move beyond "assigned work" to actively improve the quality, reliability, and performance of our systems. You will work across product, frontend, infrastructure, data, and security boundaries, making sound architectural trade-offs, communicating complex ideas clearly in an asynchronous environment, and helping define the standards for a high-scale, global product.</p> <h2>Why you’ll love this role</h2> <ul> <li><strong>High Impact: </strong>You aren't just shipping features; you are shaping the architecture of a global platform used by millions.</li> <li><strong>Technical Agency: </strong>You will influence team objectives, technical direction, and long-range goals, helping us solve problems of high scope and complexity.</li> <li><strong>Innovative Culture: </strong>You will get to experiment with and integrate agentic AI into production engineering workflows, moving beyond simple prompt engineering to build resilient, AI-assisted systems.</li> <li><strong>Autonomy: </strong>You will thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.</li> <li><strong>User-Centric Collaboration: </strong>You’ll partner closely with PMs and designers to shape requirements, ensuring every technical decision delivers genuine value to our users.</li> </ul> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Drive Technical Direction: </strong>Design and ship moderate to complex backend features with minimal guidance, making pragmatic choices between modular-monolith code, shared components, or independently operated services.</li> <li><strong>Raise the Bar: </strong>Advocate for product quality, security, availability, and performance. A primary focus for this role is building proactive data growth controls for GitLab.com, including retention and lifecycle management frameworks, enforcement of retention policies at schema-change time, and tooling that keeps database growth sustainable as AI-driven development accelerates how quickly data accumulates. You'll help teams across GitLab reason confidently about data architecture, placement, and lifecycle management, while proactively identifying saturation points in our GitLab.com infrastructure and driving corrective actions with partner teams. With the team's recent move into the Data Engineering organization, you'll also shape new scalability and data health features for self-managed customers, working hands-on with PostgreSQL and Ruby on Rails in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/22105">Data Growth Controls (retention enforcement and data lifecycle management)</a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/17719"><u><span class="textUnderline">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</span></u></a></li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/16152"><u><span class="textUnderline">Background Operations Framework</span></u></a></li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Develop and iterate backend features and data frameworks that make it safe and efficient for GitLab teams to work with data at scale across SaaS and self-managed deployments.</li> <li value="2">Design and build data retention and lifecycle management frameworks, including retention policy enforcement, bulk data removal tooling, and automated identification of tables that need retention policies.</li> <li value="3">Build shift-left guardrails, such as static analysis checks and schema-change-time enforcement, that catch unsustainable data growth patterns before they reach production.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate closely with product management, UX, frontend, infrastructure, software delivery, and analytics teams to design and ship high-performing solutions</li> <li value="5">Review and improve database-related changes from other engineers and community contributors, ensuring data integrity, safety, and performance across all deployment scenarios.</li> <li value="6">Design, build, and maintain tooling such as SQL traffic replay and background operations frameworks to proactively surface and address scalability and performance issues.</li> <li value="7">Research, design, and implement improvements to data retention and lifecycle management, database performance, scalability, and data health, including areas like soft delete strategies and database migration testing.</li> <li value="8">Document database best practices, patterns to avoid, and data architecture guidance to enable developers to make informed decisions.</li> <li value="9">Develop proactive tooling and guardrails that help developers detect and remediate potential performance and data issues early in the development lifecycle.</li> <li value="10"> </li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including high availability solutions with automatic failover and zero-downtime data migrations as well as managing large or fast-growing datasets through approaches such as data retention, archiving, partitioning, or lifecycle management.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Ruby on Rails or another Ruby framework, including designing, implementing, and reviewing backend features.</li> <li value="3">Ability to reason about software design, algorithms, and performance trade-offs at a system level.</li> <li value="4">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="5">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills and the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one".</li> <li value="6">Alignment with GitLab's values, including transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and contribution to open source.</li> <li value="7">Openness to learning and applying new tools and approaches, including transferable experience from related data, infrastructure, or developer tooling domains.</li> <li value="8">Willingness to participate in our <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/#tier-2-on-call">tier 2 dabase on-call rotation</a> in your time zone.</li> </ul> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence Group</a> is a remote, agile backend team that builds and maintains the frameworks, patterns, and tooling that enable GitLab teams to work confidently with data at scale across all application datastores. You’ll work closely with sales and internal teams to keep deals on track while protecting GitLab’s interests.</p> <p>You’ll be part of the team that helps GitLab do business every day, bringing pace, precision, and good judgment to a broad range of commercial legal work. In this hands-on role, you’ll keep the day-to-day contracting work moving while also contributing to various strategic enterprise deals across the region.</p> <p>You’ll report to the Director of Legal and work with a collaborative team that values clear advice, pragmatism, and a willingness to to roll up your sleeves. You’ll also help improve the playbooks, tools, and processes that make commercial contracting more consistent and scalable.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Manage a pipeline of commercial agreements across varying levels of complexity and stakeholder needs.</li> <li>Draft and review subscription agreements, artificial intelligence terms, regulatory annexes, professional services agreements, non-disclosure agreements, and related commercial documents.</li> <li>Negotiate contract terms directly with customer counterparts in a way that supports deal progress and protects GitLab's legal and business interests.</li> <li>Collaborate with sales teams and internal stakeholders to provide clear, timely guidance on contracting questions throughout the deal cycle.</li> <li>Assess contractual risk across your caseload and translate legal issues into practical options and recommendations for the business.</li> <li>Support sales enablement by creating practical guidance and helping sales team members understand and navigate contract terms.</li> <li>Maintain and improve team playbooks, templates, and process documentation to support consistent, scalable contracting practices.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating commercial contracts in a software or technology environment.</li> <li>Knowledge of technology-related agreements, including complex commercial arrangements, and contracts with structured regulatory or licensing considerations.</li> <li>Ability to balance business goals with legal risk using a practical, solutions-oriented approach.</li> <li>Skill in explaining contractual concepts clearly to non-legal stakeholders and external counterparts.</li> <li>Experience working across geographies and time zones, with awareness of differing commercial and regulatory norms in global contracting.</li> <li>Familiarity with Google Workspace and contract lifecycle management tools; title: Senior CX Platform Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior CX Platform Engineer, you'll help GitLab's Customer Experience (CX) teams hand real work to artificial intelligence (AI). You'll use Claude Code and GitLab Duo Agent Platform as your default development tools, designing agentic workflows and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers with production testing, security, and shared ownership. This is a software engineering role, not ticket-taking internal IT, AI evangelism disconnected from shipped code, or customer-billable Professional Services delivery.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Use Claude Code, GitLab Duo, and other coding agents as your primary development environment for planning, implementation, refactoring, testing, reviews, and documentation. Run multiple agents in parallel on well-scoped tasks, critically review their output, and own every line that reaches production.</li> <li>Build and maintain the team's agent harness, including shared AGENTS.md conventions, skills, slash commands, hooks, subagent definitions, and continuous integration checks. Measure and share what works, publish reusable patterns, and retire those that don't.</li> <li>Ship agents and multi-step workflows for account research, success planning, scoping, status reporting, and customer onboarding. Package them as skills and plugins for non-engineers using Claude, Claude in Slack, and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li>Build MCP servers and connectors for governed access to GitLab, Salesforce, Gainsight, Kantata, Thought Industries, Gong, Snowflake, and other enterprise systems. Add evaluations, tracing, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints to keep internal and customer-facing agents measurable, auditable, and safe with customer data.</li> <li>Evolve the CX Application Platform's gateway, Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, including Elastic Container Service (ECS), Relational Database Service (RDS), and Lambda, Terraform configuration, application scaffold, and deployment path. Own applications such as PS Compass, Congregate, and GitLab University and its integrations, documenting build-versus-buy and consolidate-or-sunset decisions.</li> <li>Ship production-quality Python and TypeScript through GitLab continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), with tests, observability, security review, and runbooks. Design every application for handoff, with documentation, monitoring, and shared ownership.</li> <li>Prototype with Customer Success, Digital Success, Professional Services, Education Services, and Training in days, not quarters. Help CX team members bring their own applications to production, and turn field learning into reusable reference implementations, development paths, and enablement.</li> <li>Contribute upstream to GitLab and share product feedback with Product and Engineering. Mentor engineers and non-engineers on agentic development and raise the team's code review bar.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building and operating production software, owning multi-quarter work from ambiguity to production, choosing reusable platform solutions over one-off customization where appropriate, and designing for handoff.</li> <li>Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitLab Duo, or similar on production work. You can show how they've changed what you ship and how you maintain quality.</li> <li>Experience building with large language models (LLMs) beyond chat, including tool use, MCP servers, agent loops, context and retrieval design, prompt and workflow design, and evaluations.</li> <li>Strong Python skills with FastAPI or Flask and TypeScript skills with Vue or React, including application programming interface (API) design, authentication, authorization, and secure handling of customer and business data.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with AWS ECS, RDS, and Lambda, Terraform, Docker, and applications running behind single sign-on (SSO), such as Okta.</li> <li>Experience integrating enterprise systems through Representational State Transfer (REST) and GraphQL APIs, and fluency with Git, merge requests, and CI/CD.</li> <li>Experience translating non-engineering stakeholders' workflows into technical plans and writing clear asynchronous design documents, decision records, and enablement materials. You align with GitLab's values and are willing to use GitLab for your own work.</li> <li>Optional experience includes agent harness customization; the GitLab Development Kit, Duo Agent Platform custom agents and flows, or AI Catalog publishing; enterprise agent governance and data controls; customer success, professional services, or learning platforms such as Salesforce, Gainsight, Kantata, or Thought Industries; professional services economics and customer success metrics; Snowflake or similar warehouses; and technical writing, talks, or open source contributions on agentic development.</li> </ul> <p>We welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; you don't need to meet every nice-to-have to apply.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>CX Platform Engineering builds and runs CX Applications for Customer Success, Digital Success, Professional Services, Education Services, and Training. We own the CX Application Platform's gateway and infrastructure alongside our application portfolio: GitLab University, the Foundational Onboarding Agent in GitLab Duo Agent Platform, Congregate, PS Compass, and Customer Wins. We build the first version with the people doing the work, turn what we learn into a reusable pattern, then hand it off so it runs without us. We reward leverage, not heroics, and don't leave tools dependent on one person.</p> <h4><br><br></h4><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Together you will make sure GitLab brings the right depth to the right opportunities, and that what the field learns shapes what GitLab builds next.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Set the strategy, operating model and global standards for the SME organization, aligned to the VP Global SA and GitLab's go-to-market plan.</li> <li>Build the resourcing model from product-level bookings and consumption targets. Run a structured feedback loop that shapes roadmap, launch readiness and early-access programs.</li> <li>Hire, mentor and develop regional SME Managers and, through them, the full global team.</li> <li>Own the engagement model with the regional SA Senior Directors, Post-Sales SAs and Customer Success: triage rules, coverage thresholds, the closed-won handoff to Post-Sales SAs, and escalation paths.</li> <li>Create and improve upon the processes, metrics and KPIs for SME-led technical evaluations, workshops, demos and Proofs of Value.</li> <li>Partner with CRO staff, regional sales leaders and AVPs on product-category performance, forecast risk and competitive strategy.</li> <li>Partner with Enablement to drive  field readiness for new product launches with Product Marketing and Enablement, including Duo Agent Platform, security and platform offerings.</li> <li>Build strong relationships with key customers at the technical sponsor and executive level.</li> <li>Use AI to change how the team works, including deal research, demo creation, PoV automation and knowledge sharing.</li> <li>Drive organizational transformation by finding gaps early, building structure where none exists, and leading change without waiting for top-down direction.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>5+ years second-line leadership experience (managing managers) in Solutions Architecture, Sales Engineering or a technical specialist organization.</li> <li>Experience building or scaling a specialist, overlay or global SA team in enterprise SaaS, DevSecOps, security or developer tools.</li> <li>A record of tying technical-team design to bookings and consumption outcomes, with the data to show it.</li> <li>The ability to lead through ambiguity and rapid organizational change, bringing clarity and direction while strategy is still forming.</li> <li>Strong relationships with Product and Engineering leaders, and a history of shaping roadmap from field insight.</li> <li>Fluency across the software development lifecycle, application security (SAST, DAST, SCA), cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), Kubernetes and AI-assisted development, including LLM evaluation and production deployment patterns.</li> <li>Executive presence with technical practitioners, managers and C-level stakeholders.</li> <li>Proven ability to partner across Sales, Partners, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Customer Success and Professional Services.</li> <li>A self-starting, entrepreneurial approach. You don't wait for a playbook; you write it.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>How you'll be measured</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Global product-category commit attainment and consumption growth.</li> <li>Time from technical win to first workload in customer’s production environment on SME-engaged opportunities compared with non-engaged opportunities.</li> <li>SME coverage and engagement speed on the top 10% of opportunities.</li> <li>Account Team capability lift: fewer escalations and more deals handled without an SME over time.</li> <li>Product impact: field sentiment on the product feedback process along with field-sourced requirements adopted into the roadmap.</li> <li>Team health: hiring against plan, manager development, engagement and retention.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Subject Matter Expertise (SME) organization is part of GitLab's Solutions Architecture team, a trusted technical partner for the field. teams to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities and maintain secure, up-to-date dependencies.</li> <li value="5">Manage cloud marketplace listings and integrations with major cloud providers.</li> <li value="6">Maintain and test installation, update, and upgrade documentation and processes before release.</li> <li value="7">Ensure license compliance across bundled dependencies.</li> <li value="8">Submit components and packages to partners for validation and certification.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Have used Linux build toolchains such as autotools, make, CMake, and Nix.</li> <li value="2">Have built container images and used container build tooling in production.</li> <li value="3">Have worked with Debian- and Red Hat Enterprise Linux-based systems to build <code><span class="textCode">.deb</span></code> and <code><span class="textCode">.rpm</span></code> packages and package cloud native applications.</li> <li value="4">Have used continuous integration systems, including GitLab's continuous integration feature, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or Travis CI.</li> <li value="5">Have written and maintained complex shell scripts in production environments.</li> <li value="6">Have communicated in written and spoken English in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.</li> <li value="7">Have worked with major cloud This is a unique opportunity to shape large-scale implementations that improve how customers plan, build, secure, and operate software using GitLab.</p> <h2><strong>Some examples of our solutions architects, and delivery leaders to turn complex DevSecOps transformations into clear, actionable implementation roadmaps and statements of work</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll consulting, training, success tiers, and additional solutions proactively to ensure successful outcomes and long-term customer retention</li> <li>Facilitate solutioning sessions including implementation roadmapping, enterprise strategy discussions, and executive-level requirements gathering</li> <li>Drive measurable outcomes by structuring services that support customer success metrics, accurately forecasting services bookings, and tracking key performance indicators related to bookings, margin, and attachment to strategic opportunities.</li> <li>Own the engagement lifecycle from initial discovery and pre-sales solutioning through scoping, SOW development, staffing alignment, and transition to delivery, ensuring engagements are deliverable, clearly defined, and outcome-oriented.</li> <li>Influence cross-functional teams by articulating GitLab’s professional services value proposition in the context of federal requirements and compliance frameworks, and by feeding customer insights back into sales, delivery, and practice management.</li> <li>Partner with regional sales and engagement leadership to prioritize and manage services opportunities that support critical deals and strategic initiatives, providing clear recommendations on risk management, negotiation strategies, and commercial structures.</li> <li>Foster a culture of enablement and continuous improvement by training field teams on how to position and sell professional services by sharing trends, feedback, and suggestions that improve go-to-market content and operational processes.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Demonstrated progressive experience structuring, scoping, and selling professional services engagements in the region</li> <li>Proven success operating in a pre-sales context, conducting discovery, designing outcome-oriented proposals, and developing custom statements of work (SOWs) and staffing plans for large, complex implementation projects.</li> <li>Solid understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC), DevOps practices, and cloud transformation initiatives, with the ability to connect technical solutions to mission objectives and measurable business outcomes.</li> <li>Effective communication and interpersonal skills with executive presence, able to build trusted advisor relationships with division chiefs, program managers, contracting stakeholders, and senior technical leaders.</li> <li>Highly developed facilitation, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to guide customers through acquisition processes, commercial structures, and risk mitigation strategies.</li> <li>Comfort working cross-functionally with sales, solutions architecture, delivery, and operations teams to align on deal strategy, staffing, and successful execution in a fast-paced environment.</li> <li>Capacity to work autonomously and asynchronously in a fully remote setting, managing multiple complex opportunities while maintaining accurate forecasting and consistent alignment with GitLab values and goals.</li> </ul> <p>The Professional Services Engagement Management team at GitLab is description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>An overview of this role</strong></span></h2> <p>GitLab is building the most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform, and this role will help shape how teams move from planning to code in an AI-native software development lifecycle.</p> <p>As Senior Product Manager, Source Code, you'll shape how planning and managing source code will evolve in an AI-native software development lifecycle. This role is focused on bringing planning and code closer together, so teams can move from requirements and specifications to commits, merge requests, and customer value with speed and quality.</p> <p>This area is evolving quickly. We're exploring how AI agents can use specifications, context, and human feedback to build the right thing, not just build the thing right. You'll define new product experiences for spec-driven, human-in-the loop development: how the link between planning intent and the code that implements it gets created, stays accurate as both change, and gets used at review time. The hard part is that this link decays. Code moves, specs might not follow, you will define how to make that connection self-maintaining.</p> <p>This is an ambiguous, high-impact opportunity for a product manager who has strong software development lifecycle knowledge, is comfortable working with technical teams, and wants to help create something new in DevSecOps.</p> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Define and drive product strategy for experiences that connect planning, source code management, and AI-assisted development.</li> <li>Shape workflows where teams and agents move between intent and code in both directions, so a specification can be traced to the merges that implement it and a diff can be read and reviewed against the intent behind it.</li> <li>Work with engineering, design, and other product teams to build product experiences that support human-in-the-loop and autonomous development workflows.</li> <li>Partner with teams working on demos and prototypes, including near-term work around spec-driven planning and autonomous development modes, including which decisions stay with a human and why.</li> <li>Use customer insights, product usage data, and market context to identify opportunities that can deliver customer value quickly.</li> <li>Help teams ship fast with quality, balancing near-term execution with longer-term product direction.</li> <li>Explore how planning can better account for reviewing code, reviewing test cases, and validating that work produced by agents matches the intended outcome.</li> <li>Collaborate across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI product areas to reduce friction across the software development lifecycle.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Bring</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Experience as a product manager working on developer tools, DevOps tools, source code management, planning tools, AI-native products, or related software development lifecycle products.</li> <li>Direct, hands-on experience with the source code lifecycle, including branches, merge requests, code review, CI/CD, and releases, whether as a product manager or as an engineer, along with a strong understanding of how software moves from ideas and requirements through planning, coding, review, testing, and delivery.</li> <li>Experience working with technical product areas and engineering teams, with enough technical depth to understand developer workflows and tradeoffs.</li> <li>A data-forward approach to product management, including experience using data to identify customer impact and guide prioritization.</li> <li>Comfort operating in ambiguous spaces where there may not yet be a clear market pattern or established product category.</li> <li>Experience building or shipping with AI tools and agents, not just using them, and a point of view of your own on where AI helps and where it does not across the software development lifecycle.</li> <li>Ability to think creatively about how AI changes the software development lifecycle and how product experiences should adapt.</li> <li>Strong collaboration and communication skills, especially in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>A bias toward action and the ability to help teams ship meaningful customer value quickly.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>About the team</strong></span></h2> <p>This role sits within the Product organization and will work closely with teams across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI. We are focused on helping GitLab customers plan, build, and deliver software in a faster, more connected way.</p> <p>You'll join a group that is rethinking how planning and coding should work as AI changes the speed and shape of software development. Rather than treating planning, coding, and review as separate stages, we're exploring how to bring these workflows closer together so humans and agents can collaborate more effectively.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Senior Product Manager, CRM & GTM Systems
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An Overview about the Role</strong></p> <p>We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the Lead-to-Opportunity (L2O) domain within our Salesforce and GTM technology ecosystem. This role sits at the intersection of marketing operations, sales process, and technology owning the roadmap for how leads are captured, scored, routed, and converted into pipeline, and how our broader GTM tech stack supports that motion.</p> <p>This is a foundational hire one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA model into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. You'll be both an individual contributor driving your own domain and a mentor helping BSAs grow into product manager roles. You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Internal Product Roadmap Ownership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for the Lead-to-Opportunity domain covering lead capture, enrichment, scoring, routing, conversion, opportunity and the broader GTM technology stack integrated with Salesforce</li> <li>Translate business strategy from Marketing, Sales Development, RevOps, and GTM leadership into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics</li> <li>Define the domain's strategic priorities each quarter and half, balancing net-new capability delivery, stabilization, and technical debt reduction with transparent trade-off frameworks</li> <li>Drive quarterly planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and BSAs to align capacity with roadmap commitments</li> <li>Own domain-level documentation: process maps, current-vs-future state lead lifecycle flows, and decision logs that keep stakeholders and the team aligned on scope and ownership</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary product voice for all L2O and GTM Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Marketing, Marketing Operations, SDR/BDR leadership, Sales, and RevOps</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions translating complex GTM and marketing operations requirements into actionable system specifications</li> <li>Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions</li> <li>Run structured stakeholder alignment sessions to surface trade-offs, build consensus, and drive open decisions to closure rather than letting them linger</li> <li>Represent the domain in cross-team planning and leadership reviews able to explain technical constraints to business stakeholders and business context to engineers</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team Mentorship & Capability Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as a product craft mentor and senior thought partner for the BSA team, actively upskilling analysts in product thinking, requirements structuring, acceptance criteria definition, and roadmap communication</li> <li>Model and codify what "good" looks like reusable templates, rituals (backlog grooming, roadmap reviews), and a rubric BSAs can grow against</li> <li>Give BSAs increasing ownership over pieces of the roadmap as they develop, with regular feedback and structured check-ins</li> <li>Partner with leadership to evolve the team's operating model from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how EntApps delivers business value</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead initiatives end-to-end: discovery, requirements, prioritization, solution design review, UAT, launch, and post-launch measurement</li> <li>Write and maintain clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and lead-flow and data-flow diagrams that engineering and admins can build against without ambiguity</li> <li>Manage a healthy, well-groomed backlog intake requests from Marketing and Sales Development, triage by impact and effort, and defend prioritization decisions to stakeholders</li> <li>Define success metrics per initiative (lead response time, routing accuracy, lead-to-opportunity conversion rate, data quality, SDR/BDR adoption) and report on outcomes, not just delivery</li> <li>Identify and de-risk dependencies across adjacent domains campaign operations, data enrichment vendors, opportunity handoff to sales before they block delivery</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers on Salesforce and MarTech integration design marketing automation platform to Salesforce sync, data enrichment pipelines, lead scoring and routing engines, ensuring choices hold up to governance, scale, and future roadmap needs</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on GTM platform architecture trade-offs based on deep domain knowledge</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce Sales Cloud and connected MarTech tools, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds</li> <li>Maintain domain-level R&R clarity, who owns what across US/India technical managers, BSAs, and adjacent pods and update as team and scope evolve</li> <li>Ability to engage deeply with engineering and architecture teams on API design, data modeling, and integration patterns.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years in Salesforce product management, business systems analysis, or Marketing/Revenue Operations technology roles, with demonstrated growth into product ownership</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of Lead-to-Opportunity processes; lead capture, scoring, routing, and conversion and how they connect marketing execution to sales pipeline</li> <li>Hands-on familiarity with the GTM technology stack: Salesforce Sales Cloud plus marketing automation platforms (Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot), lead scoring and routing tools, and data enrichment or intent providers</li> <li>Good Understanding of quoting process </li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders</li> <li>Proven experience leading initiatives end-to-end with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities, especially across Marketing and Sales</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs — without needing to write code</li> <li>Experience mentoring or upskilling analysts and BSAs, you enjoy developing people, not just managing tickets</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication; able to represent technical trade-offs to non-technical executives and translate business asks into clear technical requirements</li> <li>Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving structure where none exists</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted development workflows, data governance and compliance for lead data, or prior people-management experience</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>You'll be one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA function into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. The Lead-to-Opportunity domain sits at the top of GitLab's revenue funnel; the quality of data, routing, and conversion here affects every downstream system and every seller. Getting this right is not an IT problem; it's a revenue problem. infrastructure needs, and use that insight to guide implementation plans and deliverables.</li> <li>Lead migrations from legacy source code management and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) tooling, including application security tools such as Snyk, Checkmarx, Veracode, SonarQube, and GitGuardian, to GitLab CI/CD and GitLab security scanners.</li> <li>Support security-focused delivery kits, documentation, training materials, case studies, and enablement sessions.</li> <li>Partner with Training, Support, Customer Success, and Professional Services Program Managers to plan and deliver engagements.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Technical expertise</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience delivering secure enterprise continuous delivery (CI/CD) platforms with security controls.</li> <li>Experience advising on GitLab SaaS, Self-Managed, and Dedicated deployment tradeoffs for security and compliance needs.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of GitLab security scanning capabilities, including Advanced Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), Dependency Scanning, Secret Detection, and Container Scanning.</li> <li>Experience migrating application security tooling, including Snyk, Checkmarx, Veracode, SonarQube, and GitGuardian, to GitLab Security Scanners.</li> Clear, concise documentation is a big part of this job.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the policies that define how deals are booked, credited, and forecasted, including bookings rules, opportunity netting, and sales stages and exit criteria. Write them, get them approved, and make sure the field understands what changed and why.</li> <li>Identify process problems before they affect the numbers. Product, and Legal, and escalating stalled or high-severity items. </li> <li>Mature and maintain a risk register and quarterly reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into open risk, remediation progress, and trends.</li> <li>Own and mature AI risk management, including AI impact assessments, AI risk assessments, and risk treatments, to support ISO 42001 certification.</li> <li>Design, develop, and implement key risk indicators and supporting metrics for top risks in the risk register.</li> <li>Identify manual, repetitive steps in risk and TPRM workflows and personally build the automation, scripting, or AI-enabled tooling to remove them. </li> <li>Contribute to the roadmap for the risk program, incorporating new frameworks, regulatory changes, and lessons learned from past assessments.</li> <li>Monitor the internal and external risk landscape (new frameworks, threat trends, business changes) to identify and escalate emerging risks before they become findings.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in security risk management, working with security-centric risk management or compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST RMF, NIST 800-39, ISO 31000). Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF) is a plus.</li> <li>Experience designing and executing qualitative and quantitative risk analyses that translate technical risks into measurable business impact. </li> <li>A track record of driving risk assessments, risk registers, and remediation efforts to closure across IT, Procurement, Internal Audit, Legal, Product, and Engineering, in a heavily regulated or multi-entity environment.</li> <li>Experience interpreting technical control requirements and translating them for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Demonstrated bias toward automation: you've personally built scripts, workflows, or AI-enabled tooling that reduced manual risk or GRC work, not just evaluated tools conceptually. </li> <li>Comfort operating with ambiguity, managing multiple concurrent assessments, and reprioritizing under tight deadlines. </li> <li>Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to translate security risks into business risks.</li> <li>Strong understanding of cloud security, SaaS security models, and DevSecOps practices.</li> <li>Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC) are preferred but not required. </li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The <strong>Security Assurance </strong>organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk across the company. The Security Risk team sits within that group and owns third-party risk (TPRM), security risk assessments, and remediation of security findings. The Security Risk Team performs thorough, collaborative, and efficient risk assessments as well as drive risk reduction so that GitLab can achieve its goals while maintaining a high level of security. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.</p> <p>Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.</p> <p>These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats</li> <li>Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats</li> <li>Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation</li> <li>Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.</li> <li>Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous problems and shipping with minimal guidance, with the self-motivation and organizational skills suited to a remote, largely asynchronous environment</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems, and to write design proposals that bring a team to a decision</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data, including measuring false positives and missed findings</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization at scale</li> <li>Hands-on program analysis experience, such as parsing, ASTs, or data-flow analysis</li> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing and dependency scanning. We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.</p> <p>We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. reusable documentation and support content that directly influence team objectives.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales teams to shape product goals, roadmaps, and priorities while driving fixes and new features.</li> <li>Participate in regular weekday and weekend on-call rotations during daytime hours, providing emergency support for self-managed GitLab and software as a service customers and coordinating incident communications with the GitLab.com Production team.</li> <li>Participate in hiring by reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews to help grow the Support team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex, customer-facing technical cases from initial contact through triage, reproduction, bug reporting, resolution, and clear customer communication, including difficult or escalated interactions.</li> <li>Strong experience with Linux systems administration, scripting, Git, and continuous integration and continuous delivery in production or customer environments, with the ability to investigate issues at both the infrastructure and application levels.</li> <li>Ability to mentor teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions, case reviews, and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Experience technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless computing, and an understanding of how different GitLab implementations operate and affect customers.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to learn, collaborate across teams, and apply transferable skills from related technical support or engineering roles.</li> <li>Fluent Korean language skills (required)</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2>
